perfil.lede: I build generative AI applications and Python backend systems, aiming for high accuracy at the lowest possible operating cost.
bio: I am a Python Backend Developer and AI Engineer with a strong focus on scalable architectures and cost optimization (FinOps). At Docato, a B2B automation legaltech, I build generative AI applications that process, classify and extract data from court documents, and that transcribe audio.
I designed the platform that centralizes all of the company's AI microservices, cutting daily infrastructure cost by 43%.

My goal is to deliver high accuracy at the lowest operating cost: I set up rigorous tests before taking models to production and, applying the same architectural mindset, cut cloud query costs (AWS Athena) by 98.6% for a major client.

itens: Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Vertex AI, Cloud Billing)

trajetoria.organizacao: Legaltech · Remote · Automation and AI for court document processing

itens: Architected and built the centralized AI platform (modular monolith) that unified the company's projects: 43% lower daily server cost and 36% lower cloud bill, even with 17% more tasks.
Contributed to the architecture, data access layer and messaging (RabbitMQ) of a rule-based document classifier, designed with legal experts to call AI models only when needed.

Optimized the Predatory Litigation Detection application: upgraded the LLM, added retries for truncated responses and moved the system to the centralized architecture, with no dedicated server and no loss of accuracy.
Lead author of 6 AI applications for court documents: Custom Agents, Audio Transcription, Audio Analysis, Data Classifier, Generative Text AI and AI Segmenter.

Rebuilt the Data Classifier with two reader models (Claude and Gemini) and a judge called only when they disagree: accuracy from 87% to 92%, 25% lower cost per task, and heavy tasks down from up to 4h42 to 6 minutes.
Created the AI Segmenter, which splits case files of up to 20,000 pages into 16 document types using deterministic rules before AI, with 59% fewer splitting errors.
Implemented audio transcription and analysis with self-hosted Whisper, eliminating per-minute API cost, and Custom Agents validated in 31 out of 31 cases with financial sector clients.

Lead author of 14 automation applications and 7 integrations with legal systems (Projuris, Brainlaw, BC Legal, SCAE, Looplex) via REST APIs and Playwright, serving large companies in the financial, healthcare and retail sectors.
Set up cost and operations monitoring: token logging per AI call, automated reports and stuck-task alerts in Google Chat.
Built back-end APIs and integrations in PHP (Yii2) for the Psyc's platform, connecting business rules to the product interfaces.
Implemented front-end screens and components with React and Next.js, working across both front-end and back-end.

trajetoria.organizacao: EBAC (British School of Creative Arts and Technology)

projetos.resumo: The AI applications ran on 7 isolated microservice pools, with duplicated infrastructure, logs and code. I designed a modular monolith in Python where each application writes only its business logic: one RabbitMQ queue per app, history in PostgreSQL, per-queue priorities and timeouts, a centralized AI client and a shared OCR cache.
projetos.resultado: 7 pools consolidated into 1 service with 8 queues · −43% daily server cost · 722 automated tests

projetos.titulo: Custom AI Agents and Structured Extraction
projetos.resumo: A generative AI agent architecture that handles highly variable rules across clients, extracting data from court documents into validated structured outputs.
projetos.resultado: Validated in 31 out of 31 cases with financial sector clients

projetos.resumo: I rebuilt the classifier with two reader models (Claude and Gemini) and a judge model that only steps in when the readers disagree. That buys accuracy without paying for three calls on every task.
projetos.resultado: Accuracy from 87% to 92% · 25% lower cost per task · heavy tasks from up to 4h42 to 6 min

projetos.resumo: Splits court case files of up to 20,000 pages into 16 document types, applying deterministic rules before calling the AI.

A financial sector client ran up to 82 AWS Athena queries per taxpayer ID (CPF), each one scanning entire tables. I architected a daily cache: Athena processes the dataset once a day and writes Parquet (ZSTD) to S3, partitioned by CPF range and read directly with DuckDB, with no dedicated server.
projetos.resultado: 98.6% lower monthly cost (from ~US$ 19.3k to ~US$ 290) · time per CPF from 20 to 30 min down to seconds

itens.titulo: Entendendo o modificador static em Java
itens.resumo: The static modifier defines members that belong to the class, not to the instance. What that changes in shared values and method overriding.
A class cannot exist without a constructor. A piece dedicated to them, with an explanation of overloading along the way.
Classes organize variables and functions, once scattered, into a context. An introduction to the foundation of Object-Oriented Programming.
Curious behaviors that show up when learning a language. Sometimes it is a bug, sometimes something perfectly normal that is still worth understanding.
The motto that made me want to learn Java: write once, run anywhere. How the JVM makes that promise possible.

itens.titulo: Do Básico ao Essencial: A Importância da Objetividade na Programação
itens.resumo: It was a simple calculator, until suddenly it was not. On projects that grow in complexity and the value of focusing on the essentials.
